definitions.gloss: arrowroot starch; kudzu starch; kuzu powder
definitions.explanation: A fine white starch extracted from the root of the kudzu plant ({葛|くず}). Used as a thickener in Japanese cooking and as the base for traditional sweets. Prized for the smooth, glossy texture it gives to sauces and desserts.

examples.japanese: くず{粉|こ}でとろみをつける。
くず{粉|こ}を{水|みず}で{溶|と}いてから{鍋|なべ}に{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Dissolve the kuzu starch in water before adding it to the pot.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}くず{粉|こ}は{値段|ねだん}が{高|たか}いが、{仕上|しあ}がりの{食感|しょっかん}がまったく{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Pure kuzu starch is expensive, but the resulting texture is completely different.

notes:
The starch is extracted from the root of {葛|くず} (kudzu/arrowroot vine, Pueraria montana). Written as くず{粉|こ} or {葛粉|くずこ}. The くず portion is often written in hiragana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- くず{粉|こ}を{溶|と}く: to dissolve kuzu starch (in water)
- {本|ほん}くず{粉|こ}: pure kudzu starch (100% kudzu, not blended)
- くず{粉|こ}でとろみをつける: to thicken with kuzu starch
- {吉野|よしの}くず: Yoshino kuzu — the most famous producing region

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {片栗粉|かたくりこ}: potato starch — the everyday thickening starch in Japanese kitchens; cheaper and more common
- コーンスターチ: cornstarch — another thickener, used mainly in Western-style cooking
- {葛|くず}: kudzu (the plant) — the source of the starch

CULTURAL NOTE:
くず{粉|こ} is essential for traditional {和菓子|わがし} (Japanese sweets) such as {葛切|くずき}り (kuzu noodles served chilled with brown sugar syrup), {葛餅|くずもち} (kuzu mochi), and {葛湯|くずゆ} (a warm, soothing drink made by dissolving kuzu starch in hot water, traditionally given to people with colds). {吉野|よしの} in {奈良県|ならけん} is the most renowned production area. True {本|ほん}くず{粉|こ} (pure kudzu starch) is expensive, so many commercial products are blends with {甘薯|かんしょ} (sweet potato) starch.
